facts.text: In 1886, members of the Tunis, Seth, Lowe, and Cockey families christened the area 'Bay City,' a name that later evolved into Claiborne.
Today the historic Claiborne Wharf serves as a county‑owned boat launch, while a jetty built for the passenger ferry is leased from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.
The Baltimore & Eastern Shore Railroad finished a rail line from Claiborne to Easton in 1890, allowing travelers to continue on to Ocean City.
The former United Methodist Church, now Village Hall since 2010, preserves a historic building that once served as a community center.
Rich Neck Manor’s 1652 land patent marks the earliest colonial development that eventually became the village of Claiborne.
